## Why this exists

In the lecture we opened with a puzzle:

> You build an agent that reviews contracts. It does the work of three paralegals.
> It costs you **£200 a month** to run. A law firm pays **£180,000 a year** for those people.
> So… **what do you charge?**

The point of that puzzle was that there is *no single answer*. The same piece of
software can be priced anywhere from "cost plus a little" to "a share of the value it
unlocks" — a spread of **100× or more** — depending only on the **commercial model** you
choose and the **risk** you take on.

These pages let you drive the models yourself. Move the sliders, watch the price move,
and build the intuition that the framework tries to capture.

::: {.callout-note}
## Everything here runs in your browser
There is no server. The calculators run as code inside this page, so you can fork the
site, change the formulas, and host your own version on GitHub Pages for free.
:::

## A reminder on the five models

| Model | Charging basis | Risk / reward |
|---|---|---|
| **M1 · Per Seat** | Per agent "seat", benchmarked to a human FTE | Low / Low |
| **M2 · Usage** | Per token, call, or transaction | Low / Low |
| **M3 · Task** | Per completed unit of work | Low / Medium |
| **M4 · Hybrid** | Base platform fee + a usage or outcome layer | Low / Medium–High |
| **M5 · Outcome** | A share of the value delivered | Medium–High / Very High |

> The numbers in these tools are **illustrative** — calibrated to teach the *shape* of each
> model, not to quote a real deal. For live engagements, use the CoE pricing templates.
